style: Use case: product-mockup. Photorealistic commercial product photograph of a real, physically manufactured desk object, as if shot in a small studio on a medium-format digital camera with a 100mm macro lens at f/11, ISO 100. Lighting: one large soft window-like light from the upper left plus a white bounce card on the right; soft, natural, slightly directional shadows with a correct dark contact shadow where the object touches the surface. The object is a 1:40 scale model of a standard 20-foot ISO shipping container made as a real steel desk storage box (about 15 cm long, 6 cm wide, 6.5 cm tall). Accurate container construction: trapezoidal corrugated side and end walls with crisp regular ribs, a slightly recessed roof with shallow ribs, four cast corner castings at every corner with oval openings, top and bottom side rails, a pair of rear swing doors with four vertical round locking bars, each bar with a lever handle, cam keepers and retaining brackets, and visible small hinges. Material: thick sheet steel with a satin, slightly textured deep navy-blue powder-coat finish (fine orange-peel texture, NOT glossy), very slightly softened edges from coating, corner castings and locking bars in a darker graphite satin metal. Real-world manufacturing honesty: tiny tolerances, faint seam lines, subtle uneven reflections, no impossible geometry; parts must line up and be symmetrical where a real container is symmetrical. Colors natural and restrained, true-to-life white balance, low saturation. AVOID: CGI or 3D-render look, plastic toy look, glossy or mirror-like surfaces, oversaturated colors, HDR, dramatic rim light, lens flare, meaningless bokeh balls, fake depth of field, over-sharpened micro detail, cloned repeating textures, warped or melted parts. Absolutely NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO brand marks, NO stickers or labels anywhere. No people, no hands.
v1: Hero shot. The closed container box sits on a light natural oak desk surface with fine wood grain, three-quarter view from slightly above (about 25 degrees), showing one long corrugated side and the door end. On the right-hand door, at chest height of the door, a small blank rectangular brushed-aluminium plate (about 18 x 11 mm) is fixed with four tiny round rivets; the plate surface is completely plain with no engraving. Background: an out-of-focus warm off-white wall, very calm. A plain black ballpoint pen lies parallel on the desk in the lower foreground for scale. Generous negative space on the left.

The same steel container box with BOTH rear doors swung fully open (about 260 degrees, resting against the side walls), seen from a three-quarter elevated angle (about 40 degrees) so the interior is visible. Interior: walls painted the same satin navy-blue, the floor is a thin real plywood board with visible wood laminations at its edge, as in real containers. Inside, neatly stored: a short stack of plain white blank business cards, a few silver paper clips and a slim pen lying diagonally. The locking bars on the open doors show their lever handles and cam ends clearly. Placed on a matte light-grey linen desk mat. Neutral off-white background.

Close-up detail photograph, straight-on and perfectly frontal (camera axis perpendicular to the doors), of the closed door end of the steel container box, filling about 85% of the frame. Show both doors, the four vertical round locking bars with their lever handles held in retaining brackets, the cam keepers at top and bottom, the bottom corner castings with oval openings, and the corrugated door panels. On the right-hand door, centered between its two locking bars, a blank rectangular brushed-aluminium plate (about 18 x 11 mm, seen perfectly flat and frontal) fixed with four small rivets at its corners; the plate is completely plain, no engraving. Even, soft frontal light with a gentle shadow under each locking bar. Background: soft out-of-focus warm grey.

Lifestyle shot on a long light oak shelf: five identical-size steel container boxes stacked like at a port, in a stable staggered pile, two on the bottom row, two in the middle row offset, one on top, with corner castings aligning on top of each other. Each box has a different satin powder-coat colour from a restrained palette: deep navy blue, off-white, warm light grey, muted teal blue, and graphite. All doors closed, all surfaces completely plain without any marks. Soft morning window light from the left, soft shadows on the wall behind. Calm, editorial interior photograph, slight eye-level view.
v2: Doors-open shot, camera looking INTO the box through its door end. IMPORTANT STRUCTURE: the container box is a closed steel box on five sides (both long corrugated side walls, the roof and the far end wall are all solid and present); the ONLY opening is the pair of swing doors at the near end. Both doors are swung open about 180 degrees and stand flat beside the side walls, hinged at the near corner posts. Camera is placed at the door end, three-quarter view about 30 degrees to the left of the box axis and about 30 degrees above, so the viewer looks deep into the long interior. Interior: satin navy-blue corrugated inner walls, a thin plywood floor with visible laminations at the front edge. Inside, neatly stored toward the opening: a short stack of plain white blank business cards, a few silver paper clips and a slim matte silver pen lying along the length of the box. Every one of the four vertical round locking bars (two per door) has its own lever handle; all four handles at the same height. Placed on a matte light-grey linen desk mat, neutral off-white background.

Close-up detail photograph, straight-on and perfectly frontal (camera axis perpendicular to the doors), of the closed door end of the steel container box, filling about 85% of the frame. Show both doors, exactly four vertical round locking bars (two per door), and EVERY one of the four bars has its own identical lever handle, all four handles at exactly the same height in the lower third, each handle resting in a small retaining bracket; cam keepers at top and bottom of every bar; the four corner castings with oval openings; corrugated horizontal door panels. On the right-hand door, centered between its two locking bars and in the upper third, a blank rectangular brushed-aluminium plate (about 18 x 11 mm, seen perfectly flat and frontal) fixed with four small rivets at its corners; the plate is completely plain, no engraving. Even, soft frontal light from the upper left with a gentle shadow under each locking bar. Background: soft out-of-focus warm grey.
